text:
I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost:

one like a rose,

the other like a thorn.

What they stole from me

did not dispossess me;

I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost,

and I am rich in purple

and in melancholy.

Oh, how loving is the rose,

and how beloved the thorn!

Like the double outline

of twin fruits,

I have faithful happiness

and happiness lost.

translation.title: Riches
translation.editorial_note: Dicha is kept as happiness rather than luck; faithful and lost sustain the poem's paradoxical wealth.
